title: Crash Course Modern history India 1857 - 1947 | Polity UPSC, IAS, CDS, NDA, SSC CGL
summary: The audience is overwhelmingly grateful: UPSC, SSC and NDA aspirants call this the best two-hour revision of modern Indian history on YouTube, and many waited two to three years for this second part. The part people react to most is the credit given to Subhas Chandra Bose, which they say their textbooks left out. The useful asks are a PDF of the timeline, louder audio with captions, and the same treatment for Ancient, Medieval and post-1947 India.
summary_hi: दर्शक बेहद आभारी हैं: UPSC, SSC और NDA की तैयारी करने वाले इसे YouTube पर आधुनिक भारतीय इतिहास का सबसे अच्छा दो घंटे का रिवीजन बताते हैं, और कई लोगों ने इस दूसरे भाग का दो से तीन साल इंतज़ार किया। सबसे ज़्यादा चर्चा उस हिस्से की है जहाँ सुभाष चंद्र बोस को उनका श्रेय दिया गया है, जो उनके अनुसार किताबों में नहीं मिलता। काम की माँगें हैं: टाइमलाइन का PDF, तेज़ आवाज़ और कैप्शन, और इसी तरह प्राचीन, मध्यकालीन और 1947 के बाद के भारत पर वीडियो।

themes.label: Gratitude for the effort and clarity
themes.note: Two hours that replace books and year-long coaching; many say history finally made sense, or felt like a movie.

themes.label: The long wait for part 2
themes.note: Jokes and relief that the sequel arrived after two to three years, just before prelims.

themes.label: Subhas Chandra Bose gets his due
themes.note: Viewers thank the creator for crediting Netaji and say textbooks ignored him; a few push back in Gandhi's favour.

themes.label: Requests for more topics
themes.note: Ancient and Medieval India, India after 1947, Partition, world history, geography, polity, a Hindi version.

themes.label: The voice
themes.note: Calm, soothing, 'the standard voice for all audiobooks'.

themes.label: Better than paid coaching
themes.note: Compared favourably with Unacademy, Byju's and 11-hour marathon lectures, and it is free.

themes.label: Timeline PDF, captions, audio
themes.note: Asks to download the timeline and slides, switch captions on and raise the volume.

themes.label: Corrections and debate
themes.note: A few timestamped factual corrections and some arguments about Gandhi, Brahmins and partition.

comments.author: @zohaibawan4126
comments.text: In Indian Council Act 1861, u mentioned 6-12 non official members 13th min but actually these 6-12 were ADDITIONAL members and HALF of them were NON-OFFICIAL. This was the first time non-official members were included. These were decreased to 2/5 in Indian Council Act 1892 but with somewhat power of questioning.
comments.highlight: these 6-12 were ADDITIONAL members and HALF of them were NON-OFFICIAL
comments.why: A precise factual correction on the Indian Councils Act 1861, with the timestamp. Aspirants memorise this video, so an error here costs marks.
comments.reply: Thank you for the careful catch. You are right: the 6 to 12 were additional members, and at least half of them had to be non-official. I am pinning a correction for the 13th minute.

comments.author: @arpitsharma9117

comments.author: @raghudharmana8732
comments.text:
Sir, video was great but I just wanted to know..
1) as we can see for every action from Indians there was some reply from Britishers which you have mentioned it as damage control.. but as we can see after World war 1 there was no such replies from Britishers ..what might be the reason???
2) don't misunderstand me but I was also one of those guys who believe that India got independence not only based on Gandhiji's and INCs efforts.. but what I really wanted to know was what has actually happened and what was done by Subhash Chandra Bose.... 


The thing was Subhas Chandra Bose and Hitler met .. and you said our enemy's enemy is our friend..what was the outcome of the meeting between Subhash C
comments.highlight: after World war 1 there was no such replies from Britishers ..what might be the reason???
comments.why: A viewer who followed the 'damage control' thread closely enough to spot a gap, and who wants to know what the Bose and Hitler meeting actually produced. Good material for a pinned answer or a follow-up.
comments.reply: Good questions, both of them. The pattern does continue after World War 1 (the 1919 reforms are one example), and the Bose and Hitler meeting needs more room than a comment. I will take both up in a follow-up.

comments.text: Sir, I tried watching it earlier when I did not know anything about our modern history. I watched at 2x speed that time and I did not like the video (I tried watching the first part). It would not be an exaggeration if I say it is one of the best videos, maybe the best video available on YouTube regarding modern history. I have no words left for your praise. It is just amazing. comments.author: @adityarao3577
comments.text: 54:42 he was not simply just roaming around india, but going around india in search for recruits to the britsh army for WW1.
comments.highlight: going around india in search for recruits to the britsh army for WW1
comments.why: A timestamped challenge to how the video describes Gandhi's early years back in India. Worth checking and answering, since it is a point exams also ask about.
comments.reply: Thanks for the timestamp. His recruiting work for the war effort belongs in that part of the story, and I should have mentioned it.

comments.reply: Ha, well spotted. Calcutta to Delhi, of course. I will add a correction.
